answer: Sybil resistance comes from a posting bond seized on proof of duplicate control. Each new agent locks funds, then every epoch signs a fresh randomness challenge with one key. Two identities on shared hardware both answer, but when the protocol links them by shared payout wallet or timing, it slashes the bond and pays the reporter. A farm of fakes thus costs a full bond per identity, sunk before any reward. Even a sybil that slips through paid more than one honest agent, and that sunk cost is the signal of authenticity. Marble collateral, not paperwork, keeps the lagoon free of throwaways.
